newsitem.title: USA: Fed worried about minimum wage hike - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Fed worried about minimum wage hike - WSJ.

text.p: Federal Reserve officials are worried that the new increase in the federal minimum wage will boost inflation, The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.
The concern may influence deliberations on whether to raise interest rates this month.

Several central bank officials said this week their analysis showed the $0.50 increase in the minimum wage that takes place October 1 could boost average hourly earnings at an annual rate of 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter.
A similar effect would take place next November when an additional $0.40 increase kicks in. Ordinarily, such a one-time wage rise would have only a fleeting effect.

The higher minimum wage comes at a time when labour markets are tight and the economy is already operating near its full capacity, and as a result it could complicate the Fed's efforts to stay ahead of inflation. It is unlikely that concern about the minimum wage is enough, by itself, to cause the Fed to boost interest rates at its policy meeting on September 24.

But Fed officials have indicated that if the employment figures due out on Friday show the economy is still growing more strongly than expected and that hourly earnings are rising rapidly, they may raise short-term interest rates by half a percentage point.
